newsitem.title: GERMANY: Frankfurt airport steps ups anti-theft measures.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt airport steps ups anti-theft measures.

text.p: Anti-theft security measures to deter casual and organised crime have been increased at Frankfurt airport(FRA), the airport authority said.
Flughafen Frankfurt Main AG (FAG) said task forces have been established to tackle crime in air cargo, post and baggage areas.
These include representatives of FAG, Deutsche Lufthansa AG, the German post office, the German border authority BGS and customs officials.
FAG spokesman Klaus Busch told Reuters there had been no serious cases of theft at the airport but the authority wanted to improve its public image and step up staff awareness of the problem.
Several freight consignments with valuable goods had disappeared in the past, however, he said.
"There are criminals outside the airport area but of course some with criminal intentions in FAG or airlines who use the opportunity for access to post, luggage or freight," he said.
One FAG priority was to encourage staff to report suspicious activities and to name the 'black sheep' among colleagues, Busch said.
A first success of the new measures earlier this year was the arrest of a group of thieves who had stolen jewellery and money orders from the post handling section, he pointed out.
Increased car park video surveillance and patrols had led to a fall in car-related theft, he added.
In addition, access to the cargo base had been restricted by a magnetised entry card and visitor registration system.

Busch stressed there was no connection between the current security measures and the continuing investigation into alleged corruption in the building of Terminal 2. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
